To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the neutron-induced carrier removal rate and mobility degradation are consistent with a net introduction rate of /sim/20 cm/spl -1/ acceptors and /sim/200 cm/spl - 1/ acceptors plus donors in the GaAs and AlGaAs layers, respectively.

the carrier-removal rates of electrons and the 77-K mobility of 2-D electrons in AlGaAs/ GaAs heterojunctions are very sensitive to the introduction of ionized defects, and that the introduction rate is much higher in the GaAs region compared to that of the AlGaAs region.

the 2-D carrier-removal and the mobility-degradation rates are very sensitive to ionizing radiation, and that the carrier removal rate is consistent with the measured net introduction rate of acceptor-like defects, whereas the mobility degradation is consistent with the combined introduction rate of donor-like and acceptors-like defects.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the radiation-induced degradation of heterojunction field effect transistor (HFET) structures.
the effects of neutron irradiation on AlGaAs/GaN heterojunction field- effect transistor (HFET) structures.
the effects of neutron irradiation on the electrical and optical properties of GaAs/AlGaAs heterojunction devices.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

neutron radiation-induced acceptor defects in the GaAlAs and GaAs layers have very little influence on the 77-K and 300-K electron mobilities, whereas the radiation-induced donor defects have significant influence on the 300-K and 77-K electron mobilities.

the net (volume) defect production rate of /spl approx/20 cm/spl -1/ in GaAs and /spl approx/2 cm/spl -2/ in AlGaAs is responsible for the carrier-removal rates and mobility degradations, respectively.
neutron irradiation-induced defects in AlGaAs and GaAs layers have different effects on the 2D carrier concentration and mobility degradation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the neutron-induced carrier removal rate in the GaAs is consistent with the introduction rate of acceptor-like defects, whereas the mobility degradation is dominated by the introduction of the combined donor- and acceptor-like centers.

, in addition to the net introduction rate of radiation-induced acceptor-like defects, the net introduction rate for the combined donor-like/acceptor-like defects is also important for understanding the mobility degradation in the irradiated heterojunction field- effect transistors.
neutron irradiation introduces both acceptor-like and donor-like defects in the AlGaAs/GaN layer.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the 2-D carrier removal rate can be used as a good measure for the radiation-induced defect concentration, whereas the radiation-induced degradation of mobility is a better measure of the combined defect concentration.
the radiation-induced acceptors are the primary cause of mobility degradation in the GaAs channel layer of AlGaAs/GaNAs heterojunction transistors.

, for the first time, we have demonstrated the feasibility of neutron irradiation as a tool for the controlled introduction of acceptors in the channel of a GaAs-based heterojunction field effect transistor structure.
